basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/Prancer%20PenSuiteAI%20Integration/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The Prancer solution for Microsoft Sentinel enables you to ingest data from the Prancer portal for PAC and CSPM scans. Refer to [Prancer Documentation Site](https://docs.prancer.io/web/) for more information. **Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:** This solution is dependent on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in [Preview](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs: a. [Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview) b. [Azure Monitor Data Collection Rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-rule-overview) c. [Azure Functions](https://azure.microsoft.com/services/functions/#overview) (optional connectivity health-check companion, see `Data Connectors/PrancerConnectivityHealthCheck/`) **Data Connectors:** 1, **Parsers:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 13, **Hunting Queries:** 6, **Watchlists:** 1, **Playbooks:** 5 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for Prancer PenSuiteAI Integration. You can get Prancer PenSuiteAI Integration custom log data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

The Solution installs a parser that transforms the ingested data into Microsoft Sentinel normalized format. The normalized format enables better correlation of different types of data from different data sources to drive end-to-end outcomes seamlessly in security monitoring, hunting, incident investigation and response scenarios in Microsoft Sentinel.

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: CSPM/IaC High Severity Alerts From Prancer

options.text: High severity CSPM/IaC posture findings found by Prancer, across all Azure resource types (disks, flow logs, network security groups, container registries, sites, storage accounts, subnets, key vaults, virtual networks/peerings, and virtual machines). Consolidates the previous per-resource-type rule set into a single detection so coverage is expressed as one query over all Snapshots rather than one near-identical rule per Azure resource type.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: PAC high severity

options.text: High severity PAC/pentest findings found by Prancer.

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: SwarmHack High Confidence Critical Findings From Prancer

options.text: Confidence-weighted suppression rule for SwarmHack (Prancer's AI-driven autonomous adversarial pentesting engine) findings: surfaces only findings where both independent scoring signals agree the finding is real and severe (RiskScore >= 7.0 and Confidence >= 0.75), rather than alerting on RiskScore alone. Uses RiskScore/Confidence/KillChain/CrownJewels - the four PrancerFindings_CL columns populated exclusively by SwarmHack and otherwise unused by the rest of this package.

elements.name: analytic4
elements.label: CSPM-flagged resource confirmed exploitable by SwarmHack

options.text:
Joins cspm posture findings against swarmhack exploitation findings on the same Azure resource
(matched via Snapshots.id/Snapshots.reference against the swarmhack finding''s ResourceID), surfacing
cases where SwarmHack independently compromised a resource CSPM had already flagged as misconfigured.
Converts routinely-deprioritized posture debt into proven-exploited infrastructure - a correlation
that requires CSPM and AI-adversarial findings to live in the same schema/table.

elements.name: analytic5
elements.label: SwarmHack kill chain traverses a CSPM-flagged resource

options.text:
Weaker companion to the direct CSPM/SwarmHack exploited-resource correlation: flags SwarmHack findings
whose free-text KillChain path merely traverses a CSPM-flagged resource as a pivot point along the way
(lateral-movement corroboration), rather than the misconfigured resource being the final compromised
target. Matches CSPM Snapshots.path tokens against the KillChain text. VALIDATION NOTE (2026-08-11):
live production KillChain values observed so far are a flat scan-level execution-mode string (e.g. "full"),
not the per-finding multi-stage path text this rule is designed to text-match against. The query is
syntax-valid and executes safely with zero false positives against current data (confirmed live), but will
stay dormant until SwarmHack populates a genuinely descriptive per-finding KillChain value - track this
against real data before relying on this rule.

elements.name: analytic6
elements.label: Crown-jewel blast radius forces severity escalation

options.text:
Force-escalates SwarmHack findings where CrownJewels contains a high-confidence sensitive target/asset
identification (confidence >= 0.8 on at least one CrownJewels entry) to Critical, overriding the nominal
Severity - correcting for the case where Severity scores the entry vulnerability rather than the value of
what SwarmHack actually identified as reachable. Only fires when the nominal Severity is not already
Critical. NOTE: validated against real production CrownJewels data (2026-08-11) - the real per-entry shape
is {category, value, confidence, context} (e.g. category="asrep_roast_target_list"), NOT the {name, type}
asset-taxonomy shape ({domain_controller, key_vault, ...}) originally assumed in the design ADR. This rule
was corrected to use the real shape; the category value space is not yet fully characterized against
production data (only one category observed so far), so the escalation trigger uses the per-entry
`confidence` field rather than a category allowlist that would need a larger, verified category taxonomy.

elements.name: analytic7
elements.label: Kill chain decomposition - deep or dangerous-technique chains

options.text:
Decomposes KillChain''s free-text stage-arrow format ("Stage A via/to detail -> Stage B via/to detail -> ...")
into a per-finding, per-stage MITRE tactic/technique chain - replacing a static, rule-level, identical-
for-every-finding tactic tag with genuine per-finding mapping. Flags kill chains that are either deep
(4+ stages) or contain a dangerous technique marker (Mimikatz, DCSync, Golden/Silver Ticket, Kerberoast,
ADCS ESC1/2/8, NTDS.dit, Pass-the-Hash). VALIDATION NOTE (2026-08-11): live-tested against real production
data - the query executes cleanly and correctly returns zero matches today, because observed KillChain
values are a flat scan-level execution-mode string ("full"), not a per-finding stage-arrow path. Safe to
ship (no errors, no false positives), but functionally dormant until SwarmHack populates a real per-finding
narrative in KillChain - revisit once that data is confirmed available.

elements.name: analytic8
elements.label: SAST finding in dangerous-CWE allowlist with evidence

options.text:
Flags DeviceProduct == sast findings scoped to a curated dangerous-CWE allowlist (SQL Injection=89,
XSS=79, Hardcoded Credentials=798, Broken/Risky Crypto=327, Path Traversal=22, SSRF=918, Insecure
Deserialization=502) that also carry non-empty AlertEvidence, instead of alerting on every SAST finding
regardless of class or evidence quality.

elements.name: analytic9
elements.label: SCA critical-unpatched and org-wide blast-radius findings

options.text:
Two SCA (DeviceProduct == sca) cases combined into one rule: (1) unpatched-critical-no-fix - CVSSScore
>= 9 with no Solution and no RemediationDescription, i.e. no compensating control is documented, not
just "update the package"; (2) org-wide blast radius - the same vulnerable Title/CweId recurring across
5+ distinct ConfigIds, i.e. a shared dependency or base-image problem invisible at single-finding
severity thresholds.

elements.name: analytic10
elements.label: DAST confirmed reflected exploitation

options.text:
Flags DeviceProduct == dast findings where the actual injected payload marker (AlertEvidence) appears
verbatim in both RequestBody and ResponseBody - proof the payload was both sent and reflected back,
rather than a header/heuristic-only match.

elements.name: analytic11
elements.label: Critical/High findings persisting across scan cycles unremediated

options.text:
Reframes the finding store from a discovery tool into an accountability tool: flags Critical/High
(SeverityRank <= 2) findings that recur across 3 or more distinct ScanIds for the same ConfigId/Title/
CweId over a 30-day window, i.e. survived multiple scan cycles unremediated. Uses first/last-seen
aggregation to surface how long each finding has been outstanding.

elements.name: analytic12
elements.label: Data-quality degradation spike by ScanType

options.text:
Meta-alert monitoring the rate of IsDataQualityIssue-flagged findings per ScanType for spikes against
a trailing 7-day baseline, surfaced alongside ScannerVersion so a scanner-release regression can be
correlated directly rather than requiring someone to notice a slow-moving workbook trend. This is an
operational-telemetry rule, not an attacker-technique detection - tactics/techniques are intentionally
left unmapped.

elements.name: analytic13
elements.label: Finding touches a watchlist-declared crown-jewel asset

options.text:
Escalates ANY finding - not just SwarmHack findings - whose ResourceID or ResourceUrl matches an asset a
customer has declared in the "Prancer Crown Jewel Assets" watchlist (see Watchlists/CrownJewelAssets.json),
to at least that asset''s declared CriticalityTier. This is the customer-declared counterpart to
CrownJewel_Severity_Escalation.yaml (which only fires on SwarmHack''s own in-the-moment discoveries): it
makes crown-jewel-aware prioritization useful for every ScanType/DeviceProduct - SAST/SCA/DAST/CSPM/IaC
findings included - even for customers who have never run a SwarmHack engagement, directly addressing the
ADR''s stated goal of making crown-jewel content valuable independent of SwarmHack engagement history.
Only fires when the watchlist-declared tier is strictly higher than the finding''s nominal Severity.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: Hunting query for failed CSPM scan items

options.text: Finds all failed CSPM control evaluations ingested by Prancer, expanded to one row per affected Azure resource for triage. This hunting query depends on PrancerLogData data connector (PrancerFindings_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: Hunting query for high severity PAC findings

options.text: Finds high and critical severity PenSuiteAI pentest findings from Prancer, with full request/response and remediation context, in one place. This hunting query depends on PrancerLogData data connector (PrancerFindings_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery3
elements.label: Kill chain stage-by-stage MITRE decomposition (all chains)

options.text:
Companion hunting query to the KillChain_MITRE_Decomposition analytic rule: decomposes every SwarmHack
KillChain (not just deep/dangerous ones) into its individual stages for free-form analyst review, one
row per stage, without the rule's deep-chain/dangerous-technique pre-filter. VALIDATION NOTE (2026-08-11):
live production KillChain values observed so far are a flat scan-level execution-mode string ("full"), not
a per-finding path - this query is safe (runs cleanly against real data) but returns one degenerate
single-stage row per finding today rather than a real multi-stage breakdown, until SwarmHack populates a
richer per-finding value. This hunting query depends on PrancerLogData data connector (PrancerFindings_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery4
elements.label: Multi-scanner MITRE technique corroboration

options.text:
Correlates MitreIds across different ScanTypes for the same ConfigId within a rolling 14-day window,
surfacing independent corroborating evidence of a plausible attack path built purely from SAST/SCA/CSPM
agreement. Requires no SwarmHack data at all, so it has standalone value for customers who haven't
licensed the SwarmHack module. This hunting query depends on PrancerLogData data connector (PrancerFindings_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery5
elements.label: Finding persistence tracker (all severities)

options.text:
Broader, exploration-oriented companion to the Finding_Persistence_Tracker analytic rule: surfaces
findings recurring across 2 or more distinct ScanIds for the same ConfigId/Title/CweId over a 30-day
window at any severity (not just Critical/High), with SeverityRank included so analysts can sort/filter
interactively rather than relying on the rule's fixed Critical/High threshold. This hunting query depends on PrancerLogData data connector (PrancerFindings_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery6
elements.label: RiskScore/Confidence divergence triage queue

options.text:
Surfaces SwarmHack findings where RiskScore and Confidence disagree: high RiskScore with low Confidence
needs manual verification before it's trusted, while low RiskScore with high Confidence may be
systematically underrated. A calibration-monitoring query that only makes sense because SwarmHack has
two independent confidence axes to diverge - no competitor in this space has both. This hunting query depends on PrancerLogData data connector (PrancerFindings_CL Parser or Table)

Microsoft Sentinel watchlists enable the collection of data from external data sources for correlation with the events in your Microsoft Sentinel environment. Once created, you can use watchlists in your search, detection rules, threat hunting, and response playbooks. Watchlists are stored in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace as name-value pairs and are cached for optimal query performance and low latency. Once deployment is successful, the installed watchlists will be available in the Watchlists blade under 'My Watchlists'.

elements.name: watchlist1
elements.label: Prancer Crown Jewel Assets

options.text: Customer-declared inventory of business-critical ("crown jewel") assets, keyed by resource identifier. Populate this watchlist with your own hostnames/resource IDs, criticality tier, category, and owning team so Prancer's crown-jewel-aware analytic rules and workbook tiles can prioritize findings even without a prior SwarmHack engagement.

This solution installs the Playbook templates to help implement your Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) operations. After installing the solution, these will be deployed under Playbook Templates in the Automation blade in Microsoft Sentinel. They can be configured and managed from the Manage solution view in Content Hub.
